chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Hasan ibn Mattil narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is more Honorable than obliging people to do what they do not have the strength to do. And Allah is Mightier than allowing something to exist in His Rule that He does not intend.

key_terms.يُطِيقُونَهُ: They have the strength/capacity for it

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about God's capacity to burden humans and His control over His kingdom?
ai.summary: In the context of the debate between the Akhbaris and Usulis regarding divine decree, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to refute the Jahmiyyah and early determinists who claimed God forces actions, thereby preserving human agency (ikhtiyar). It establishes that God’s generosity ensures obligations are within human capacity, while His absolute power guarantees that no event in His dominion occurs against His will, balancing predestination with free will.
